topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows
lecture_lines: Vectors are arrows with magnitude and direction.
Vector addition uses the tip-to-tail method.
Scalar multiplication scales the arrow's length.
animations: Draw a vector arrow from origin labeled v in #FF5733.
Label the vector with coordinates (x, y) in #FFFFFF.
Animate the vector stretching to double its length.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
lecture_lines: Span is the set of all reachable points.
Span creates a 'coverage area' on a grid.
animations: Show two basis vectors i-hat and j-hat in #33FF57.
Draw scalar multiples of these vectors in #33FF57.
Add them together to form a new vector in #FF33FF.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: Redundancy
lecture_lines: Linear dependence means having redundant vectors.
Redundant vectors don't add new dimensions.
animations: Display two vectors pointing in the same direction in #3357FF.
Animate one vector fading out to show it's redundant.
Highlight the remaining vector as the essential direction.

sections.title: Bases: The Minimal Blueprint
lecture_lines: A basis spans the entire space.
Basis vectors are also linearly independent.
A basis is the minimal blueprint required.
animations: Visualize a set of vectors spanning the entire 2D plane.
Highlight only the minimum number needed for the span.
Label this minimal set as a 'Basis' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Summary and Visualization
lecture_lines: Span defines our total reachable area.
Linear dependence points out wasted effort.
A basis is the efficient coordinate system.
animations: Show the core concepts together in a summary view.
Flash all key vectors labeled in the previous sections.
Fade out all elements to transition to conclusion.
